1596510.name: PARK PRESIDIO CAPITAL LLC
1596510.who: San Francisco hedge fund adviser founded May 2013, owned and controlled by Lee T. Hicks; co-founded with Jan Koerner, both former managing directors at Farallon Capital. 1601407.name: Troy Asset Management Ltd
1601407.who: London boutique (taml.co.uk) whose flagship Trojan Fund, launched 31 May 2001, is run by co-founder Sebastian Lyon (30+ years multi-asset experience) with Charlotte Yonge. Capital-preservation, multi-asset style: quality equities (Visa, Alphabet, Chubb, CN Rail, Agilent) plus index-linked bonds, gold and cash. Reg AUM ~$14.7B; SEC-registered for institutional/pooled clients only.
1601407.terms: Vehicles: UK OEIC funds (Trojan Fund, ISIN GB00B05M9S10; also 'Trojan Fund X Income' share class per Morningstar) sold via UK platforms; in the US only institutional/pooled clients per Form ADV. Fee schedule/OCF not found; minimum not found. Not stated to accept US individual clients.
1601407.track_record: Firm-stated (via PAM Insight): Trojan Fund +230.3% from 31 May 2001 to 28 Feb 2019 vs +47.9% cash and +156.1% FTSE All-Share. Hargreaves Lansdown and Trustnet describe it as 'slow and steady' / 'unspectacular performer still worth buying'. Our 13F-implied 2-yr return: +19.1% (excess -0.4%, clone +7.6%).
1601407.good: Long record of low-volatility, drawdown-conscious returns since 2001; HL notes strong risk-adjusted returns and additive use of inflation-linked bonds and cash; stable manager tenure.
1601407.bad: Deliberately cautious ('more cautious than ever' per HL) so it lags in strong bull markets; Trustnet labels it 'unspectacular'; UK-domiciled funds are not readily purchasable by US persons.
1601407.how_to_engage: US individuals: not available (institutional-only per ADV; UK OEIC). UK investors buy Trojan Fund on platforms. Contact +44 (0)20 7499 4030 to ask about US-eligible vehicles.

1026720.name: WELLCOME TRUST LTD (THE) as trustee of the WELLCOME TRUST
1026720.who: London-based charitable foundation endowment (~£37.6bn portfolio) funding health research; in-house investment team long led by CIO Nick Moakes, who retired end-March 2025 after 17 years. Lisha Patel and Fabian Thehos became Managing Partners and Co-CIOs from 1 April 2025. Runs a diversified portfolio; US 13F shows quality mega-caps (Visa, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, Linde). Not an adviser — no Form ADV.

Hearts & Minds piece credits Moakes' long-horizon '100-year bet' as paying off (no figures seen). Our 13F-implied 2-yr return: +8.7% (excess -10.8%, clone +3.0%).
1026720.good: Regarded for patient, multi-decade horizon and cautious positioning (growing cash pile 'waiting for opportunity').
1026720.bad: Recent one-year return modest (5.2%); CIO transition in 2025; 13F is only the US-listed slice of a global multi-asset book.
1026720.how_to_engage: Not available. Cannot be hired or invested in; 13F can only be observed.

1606152.name: Hikari Power Ltd
1606152.who: Tokyo investment vehicle that is the largest shareholder of Hikari Tsushin, Inc., a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed holding company founded 1988 by Yasumitsu Shigeta, who rebuilt it after a ~99% share-price collapse in 2000. Since ~2010 the group runs a Berkshire-inspired capital-allocation model: a core distribution business plus a large listed-equity portfolio. Hikari Power's 13F (51 positions, ~$1.2B) is ~half Berkshire Class A (783 shares) plus Berkshire-style names (Linde, J&J, Exxon, Visa). No Form ADV.
1606152.terms: Not an adviser. Indirect route only: buy Hikari Tsushin shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (no fees/minimum concept). No US-listed vehicle found.
1606152.track_record: Per MOI Global/Latticework write-ups (Apr 2026): group equity portfolio (cost ~¥830bn) sits on ~$4bn gain, 8-year IRR ~18% vs ~11% for TOPIX; over 15 years operating profit compounded >20%, book value and dividends ~17%, ROE >16%, share count down 18%. Third-party analyst claims, unaudited. Our 13F-implied 2-yr return: +16.8% (excess -2.7%, clone +8.0%).
1606152.good: Long compounding record; Berkshire-style discipline; management is founder-controlled with heavy ownership.
1606152.bad: Portfolio funded with ~$6bn of long-dated near-zero-rate yen debt (leverage/rate risk); 500–600 small Japanese positions plus an operating business make it an unusual proxy; founder succession (son Mitsutoki runs a separate book).
1606152.ugly: The 2000 collapse (~99% drawdown) is historical; no current regulatory actions found in sources seen.
1606152.how_to_engage: Not available as a manager. Exposure only via Hikari Tsushin common stock on the TSE through a broker with Japan access (IBKR supports TSE).

1590531.name: Foxhaven Asset Management, LP
1590531.who: Charlottesville, VA hedge fund founded April 2013 by Michael (Mike) Pausic (co-founder, principal, portfolio manager; University of Virginia; began long/short equity analysis work as an undergraduate). Invests in publicly traded and privately held equities, growth/quality bias (MercadoLibre, Amazon, Hilton, Ferguson, Alphabet; 14 positions). Form ADV (27 Mar 2024): 5 clients, $5.6B discretionary assets; manifest reg AUM ~$6.5B across 3 private funds.
1590531.terms: Vehicle: three private hedge funds; no individual accounts. Fee schedule not found; minimum not found; no statement on accepting new investors found.
1590531.track_record: No firm-reported returns found. Our 13F-implied 2-yr return: +7.3% (excess -12.2%, clone -3.3%).
1590531.good: Sizeable institutional following (AUM grew to ~$6.5B from launch in 2013); concentrated in well-known compounders; also invests in private companies (e.g., 13G filing on Duolingo, 2022).

1590531.how_to_engage: Private funds only; minimum not published (likely institutional-scale given 5 clients / $5.6B). Call (434) 326-5300 or foxhavencap.com.

1336528.name: Pershing Square Capital Management, L.P.
1336528.who: Bill Ackman founded Pershing Square in 2004 in New York. Concentrated activist/quality large-cap long equity, roughly 11 US positions (Brookfield, Amazon, Uber, Microsoft, Restaurant Brands). In April 2026 the manager listed as Pershing Square Inc. (NYSE: PS) alongside a new closed-end fund, Pershing Square USA (NYSE: PSUS). Manifest CRD 132982 and the New York address match the 13F filer.
1336528.terms: ADV shows 4 private funds and no individual accounts; private-fund fee schedule not found. Listed alternatives: PSUS, a closed-end fund that IPO'd 29 Apr 2026 at $50/share raising $5bn, charging a management fee of 0.50% quarterly (2.0% annualized) with no performance fee; manager shares trade as PS. Europe-listed Pershing Square Holdings also exists. No statement found on accepting new private-fund clients.
1336528.track_record: Firm-reported and press-cited: 15.9% annualized since 2004 through end-2025 versus about 10.7% for the S&P 500; cumulative net returns above 2,600% vs roughly 836% (self-reported). Ackman has separately claimed about 20% gross annualized since inception. A Motley Fool tally puts the trailing 10-year return at 164.1% vs 253.6% for the S&P 500. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: -1.2%, about 20.7 points behind benchmark.
1336528.good: Credited for deep, concentrated research positions and a strong multi-decade compounding record since 2004, and for building permanent-capital vehicles that remove redemption pressure from a highly concentrated book.
1336528.bad: Trailing 10-year returns lag the S&P 500 per third-party tallies; acute key-person dependence on Ackman; only 11 positions; PSUS traded roughly 20% below NAV in 2026 with press attributing part of the discount to the 2% fee.
1336528.ugly: December 2017: Pershing Square agreed to pay $193.75M (Valeant $96.25M; $290M total) to settle Allergan shareholder claims that it traded on information about Valeant's 2014 hostile bid. The manifest records 3 Form ADV disclosure items, which we did not review individually.
1336528.how_to_engage: The private funds are effectively closed to an individual at $1.5M (no individual accounts on the ADV, minimum not disclosed). The practical route is buying PSUS or PS on the NYSE through an ordinary brokerage account, or Pershing Square Holdings in Amsterdam. No SMA option.

1167483.name: TIGER GLOBAL MANAGEMENT LLC
1167483.who: Chase Coleman III founded Tiger Global in 2001 in New York after working at Julian Robertson's Tiger Management. Research-driven, long-horizon investing in high-quality growth and technology companies across public and private markets; the public book spans long/short, long-only and crossover strategies. Top 13F names are Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon, TSMC and Meta. Manifest CRD 160318 and New York address match the 13F filer.
1167483.terms: ADV shows 38 private funds (10 hedge) and no individual accounts, so access is via fund subscription only. Fee schedule and minimums not found; press reported the firm cut fees for flagship investors in 2022 after losses. No retail ticker. No statement found on whether the funds are open to new investors.
1167483.track_record: Press-reported: the flagship long/short fund fell roughly 56% in 2022, one of the largest single-year hedge fund losses on record, then gained 28.5% in 2023, with the long-only fund up 20.4% and further gains in 2024. Venture holdings were written down about 33% in 2022. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +14.4%, about 5.1 points behind benchmark.
1167483.good: Credited with early, large-scale positions in dominant technology and AI franchises and with an unusually deep public-plus-private research platform; the pre-2021 long-run record was among the strongest in the industry.
1167483.bad: The 2021-22 drawdown was severe and only partly recovered; venture fundraising fell short (a 2024 fund closed at $2.2bn against a $6bn target); heavy growth-tech factor concentration; key-person risk on Coleman.
1167483.ugly: The manifest records 1 Form ADV disclosure item; we did not identify any specific dated regulatory action, lawsuit or enforcement matter in our searches. Check IAPD directly before relying on this.
1167483.how_to_engage: Not practically available to an individual at $1.5M: private funds only, no separately managed accounts, and no disclosed minimum (institutional hedge fund minimums are typically far above $1.5M). The only realistic exposure is observing the 13F holdings.

1135730.name: COATUE MANAGEMENT LLC
1135730.who: Philippe Laffont, with his brother Thomas, founded Coatue in 1999 in New York, launching the first hedge fund with $45M. Laffont is a Tiger Management alumnus. The firm invests in technology, media and telecom plus consumer and healthcare, across public and private markets, with a heavy AI orientation. Manifest CRD 157910 and New York address match the 13F filer.
1135730.terms: ADV shows 146 private funds. Retail-adjacent vehicle: the Coatue Innovation Fund (CTEK), a registered tender-offer closed-end fund launched May 2025, holding 50-80% public tech and 20-50% private companies with quarterly redemptions. Minimum $50,000 for Class S and D shares, $1,000,000 for Class I; buyers must be accredited investors and qualified clients. Reported fees: 1.25% management fee plus an incentive fee (2.07% cited).
1135730.track_record: Third-party 13F-based tallies cite roughly +294% since Q3 2015 versus about +107% for the S&P 500; these are not audited fund returns. CTEK reportedly reached about $10.5bn NAV, with Anthropic, Revolut, OpenAI and Stripe among top private positions. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +25.4%, about 5.9 points ahead of benchmark, the strongest in this batch alongside Hyperion.
1135730.good: A long-tenured technology franchise with a strong public-equity record and unusual access to late-stage private AI companies, now packaged into a vehicle open to accredited investors rather than institutions only.
1135730.bad: Very high turnover (about 54% per quarter) makes 13F-copying unreliable. CTEK's private sleeve is manager-valued and illiquid with only quarterly liquidity, and the fee stack plus concentrated AI/tech factor exposure add risk.
1135730.how_to_engage: CTEK is the realistic route at $1.5M: $50,000 minimum for Class S or D shares through a broker or advisor platform, subject to accredited-investor and qualified-client status. The hedge funds themselves show no individual accounts on the ADV. Read the CTEK prospectus on valuation and redemption limits first.

1532262.name: Greenbrier Partners Capital Management, LLC
1532262.who: Dallas, Texas SEC-registered adviser (CRD 160830) running one concentrated, long-biased equity hedge fund of about 11 positions (Apple, Meta, Costco, Alphabet, Amazon), with a 3-5 person team. Named principal not confirmed: a fund database lists Herbert R. Kuppin as chief compliance officer, while a Bloomberg profile ties Lane Kasselman to a similarly named 'Greenbrier Partners' that appears to be a different (communications) firm. A directory's '1985' founding date conflicts with the 2011-12 CRD/CIK vintage, and an older unrelated filer 'Greenbrier Partners Ltd' (CIK 905770) also exists.
1532262.terms: One private fund; no individual accounts on the ADV. Fee schedule not found. Minimum not found. No public statement found on accepting new investors, and the manifest lists no website.
1532262.track_record: No audited or firm-published performance found. Third-party 13F trackers show a portfolio value of about $1.33bn at 30 Jun 2026, up slightly from the prior quarter. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +19.8%, roughly in line with benchmark (+0.3 points), on very low turnover of about 4.6% per quarter.
1532262.good: A highly concentrated, very low-turnover portfolio of quality mega-cap compounders that has roughly matched the benchmark over our two-year window without evident style drift.
1532262.bad: Almost no public disclosure: no website in the manifest, no published track record, and no confirmed portfolio manager. Single-fund, small-team structure concentrates key-person risk, and the identity confusion above is itself a diligence obstacle.
1532262.how_to_engage: Not accessible through any public vehicle. The only route is contacting the firm at 214-720-2060 about the private fund; the minimum is undisclosed and may exceed $1.5M. Confirm the firm's identity and principals on IAPD (CRD 160830) before any contact, given the name collisions noted above.

1484150.name: Lindsell Train Ltd
1484150.who: London boutique founded in 2000 by Michael Lindsell and Nick Train, both with more than three decades of experience. Very low-turnover, highly concentrated 'quality' investing in durable consumer brands and franchises; the Global Equity fund launched in 2011. The US 13F book holds about 27 names (TKO Group, Alphabet, Intuit, Disney, Thermo Fisher). Manifest CRD 158323 and London address match the 13F filer.
1484150.terms: UK-domiciled OEICs (WS Lindsell Train UK Equity, Lindsell Train Global Equity) sold through UK platforms, plus the London-listed Lindsell Train Investment Trust (LSE: LTI). Two private funds appear on the US ADV with no US individual accounts. Fee schedule not found. No statement found on accepting new clients.
1484150.track_record: Third-party data: the Global Equity fund returned -0.7% in 2025 against +12.8% for the MSCI World, with five-year annualized returns to December 2025 of 2.9% versus 12.5% for the benchmark; the fund fell to the third quartile of the IA Global sector. LTI traded at a 14.7% discount to NAV, averaging 19.7% over the 12 months to 28 Feb 2025. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +9.4%, about 10.1 points behind.
1484150.good: A genuinely differentiated, patient, low-turnover quality process run consistently for over two decades by its founders, who have not abandoned the approach through a prolonged drawdown.
1484150.bad: Sustained underperformance: firm assets fell from £24.6bn in June 2021 to £8.3bn by December 2025. Acute key-person risk on Nick Train, and LTI's own NAV includes a large stake in the management company (27.3% at 31 Jan 2025), which links trust performance to further outflows.
1484150.how_to_engage: Awkward for a US investor: the UK OEICs are generally not sold to US residents, and LTI is a UK-listed investment trust that would need a broker with LSE access and raises non-US fund tax considerations. No SMA offering. Firm phone +44 20 7808 1210; lindselltrain.com.

1963404.name: Gavilan Investment Partners LLC
1963404.who: Louis Chang founded Gavilan Investment Partners, based in Burlingame, California; the firm dates to around 2020 and began filing 13Fs in 2023. Chang previously spent 14 years as a partner and sector head at Criterion Capital Management, a San Francisco TMT-focused long/short fund, and was a senior advisor at Facebook from 2019 to 2020; he attended Stanford. Concentrated growth and consumer-internet book of about 14 positions.
1963404.terms: One private hedge fund; no individual accounts on the ADV. Fee schedule not found. Minimum not found. No public statement found on accepting new investors. Website gavilanpartners.com; phone 650-334-4990.
1963404.track_record: No audited or firm-published performance found; the firm has only filed 13Fs since 2023. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +24.2%, about 4.7 points ahead of benchmark, on roughly $372M of reported US equity against $515M regulatory AUM, with low turnover near 5.5% per quarter. Chang presented an investment idea at the 2025 Sohn San Francisco conference.
1963404.good: Strong 13F-implied results from a concentrated, low-turnover portfolio (Amazon, Meta, MercadoLibre, Carvana, Coupang), run by a manager with a long prior record as a technology sector specialist.
1963404.bad: Very short standalone history and small asset base; single-manager, single-fund key-person risk; concentration in high-beta consumer-internet names means the two-year figure may reflect factor exposure as much as skill.
1963404.how_to_engage: Private fund only. Contact through gavilanpartners.com or 650-334-4990. No minimum was disclosed anywhere we looked; hedge fund minimums commonly start at $1M and could exceed $1.5M, so confirm before spending diligence time.

2040608.name: Camrose Capital Investment Partners LLP
2040608.who: London LLP incorporated 15 January 2024 (Companies House OC450608), registered at 21a Kingly Street, Carnaby. Chief investment officer is Edward Charles ('Teddy') Molson, previously an investment analyst at Egerton Capital (UK) from 2013 to 2024. Companies House also records Christopher Patrick Hickey and Yavuz Arikan. The US 13F book is a concentrated set of about 10 quality compounders: Core & Main, Hilton, S&P Global, Mastercard, Texas Instruments.
2040608.terms: Exempt reporting adviser in the US, meaning private funds only and no retail accounts; the manifest shows $0 regulatory AUM on the US filing. One private fund. Fee schedule not found. Minimum not found. No statement found on accepting new investors.
2040608.track_record: Under two years of operating history and no audited or published performance found; a third-party 13F site cited roughly $305M AUM, while the manifest shows $764M of reported US equity. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +0.1%, about 10.9 points behind benchmark, with turnover of 2.0% per quarter. That window largely predates the fund's life, so treat the figure as unreliable.
2040608.good: A pedigreed launch out of Egerton Capital, a long-established London quality-growth manager, running an extremely low-turnover portfolio of high-return compounders.
2040608.bad: Brand-new firm with no verifiable track record and one key person; exempt-reporting status means minimal ongoing US public disclosure; our two-year measure lags materially and cannot yet be interpreted as skill or lack of it.
2040608.how_to_engage: Not available to a US individual through any public vehicle; UK/offshore private fund only, with no retail accounts. Contact camrosecapital.com or +44 20 4603 3430. Minimum is undisclosed and, for a new institutional launch, likely well above $1.5M.

1619844.name: Hyperion Asset Management Ltd
1619844.who: Brisbane, Queensland growth manager (AFSL 238380) with Mark Arnold as chief investment officer and Jason Orthman as deputy CIO and lead portfolio manager. Runs very concentrated Australian and global growth portfolios in structurally advantaged businesses; top 13F names are Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Arm. Fund research and commentary are distributed through Pinnacle Investment Management's multi-affiliate platform.
1619844.terms: Australian unit trusts plus an ASX-listed active ETF, Hyperion Global Growth Companies Fund (Managed Fund), ASX ticker HYGG. Reported Global Growth fees: 0.70% management fee plus a 20% performance fee above the benchmark. The US ADV records 39 high-net-worth individual accounts and portfolio management for individuals, so it does take direct clients; US account minimum not found.
1619844.track_record: Firm and press figures (self-reported): Global Growth returned 23.5% annualized from June 2014 inception to November 2020 and gained over 46% after fees in 2020 against a 5.7% benchmark; it returned 47.3% in the year to June 2025, more than 29 points ahead. June 2026 was +0.3%, 2.8 points behind, and HYGG fell about 27% from its 29 Oct 2025 high. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +25.0%, about 5.5 points ahead.
1619844.good: Credited with net-of-fee alpha across multiple products, which is uncommon, driven by a disciplined long-horizon process for identifying rare high-growth businesses.
1619844.bad: Extreme concentration and factor risk: about 22 holdings with Tesla near 12.6% and single positions up to 13%, producing large drawdowns such as the ~27% fall from the October 2025 peak. The 20% performance fee adds cost in strong years.
1619844.how_to_engage: The practical route at $1.5M is buying HYGG on the ASX through a broker with Australian market access; note that a foreign-domiciled fund raises non-US tax reporting questions for a US investor, so check with a tax adviser first. The firm also takes high-net-worth mandates directly; phone 1300 497 374, hyperion.com.au.

1592579.name: Trinity Street Asset Management LLP
1592579.who: London-based international and global equity specialist founded in 2002 by Richard Bruce, who remains founder and chief investment officer. Runs concentrated long-only portfolios of roughly 30-35 stocks in companies undergoing positive, under-recognized structural change; about $9.5bn AUM at December 2025, with the majority managed for US-based institutional clients. iM Global Partner has made a strategic investment in the firm.
1592579.terms: Two private funds on the US ADV and no individual accounts, so no direct retail route. Indirect access: sub-adviser to the BBH Partner Fund - International Equity since 19 August 2023 (a multi-manager fund), and manager of the Luxembourg-domiciled iMGP Trinity Street Global Equity Fund, whose I USD PR2 class carries a 0.96% ongoing charge. Direct fee schedule and minimum not found.
1592579.track_record: No audited long-term return series was found in our searches; the strategy dates to 2004. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: -10.8%, about 30.3 points behind benchmark. Caveat: the US 13F book (TSMC, Infosys, Ryanair, HDFC Bank, ICON) captures only the US-reportable slice of an international mandate benchmarked against non-US indices, so that comparison is not a fair read of the strategy.
1592579.good: A long-tenured non-US equity specialist chosen as a sub-adviser by institutional allocators such as Brown Brothers Harriman and iM Global Partner, with a stable founder-led process in place for two decades.
1592579.bad: Weak results over our measurement window, and international mandates broadly have lagged US-heavy benchmarks for years; key-person risk on Richard Bruce; direct access is institutional only.
1592579.ugly: The manifest records 1 Form ADV disclosure item; we found no specific dated regulatory action, lawsuit or enforcement matter in our searches. Verify on IAPD (CRD 152728) before relying on this.
1592579.how_to_engage: For an individual, the practical route is the BBH Partner Fund - International Equity if your platform offers it, noting Trinity Street is only one of several sub-advisers there, or the Luxembourg iMGP fund if you have access to offshore share classes. A direct mandate is institutional and would far exceed $1.5M.

1657428.name: Manitou Investment Management Ltd.
1657428.who: Independent, owner-operated investment manager in Toronto, Ontario, founded in 1999. Crunchbase lists Stephen R. Scotchmer as founder; we could not corroborate that elsewhere, so treat the name as unconfirmed. Serves both private clients and institutions (endowments, foundations, corporations, pension plans). The 13F book is a diversified quality large-cap portfolio of about 52 names led by Berkshire Hathaway, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Roper.
1657428.terms: Separately managed accounts, plus a pooled vehicle (Manitou Partners Registered Fund) referenced in Ontario Securities Commission filings. Per an OSC decision, the minimum managed account size is generally $2 million, waivable at the firm's discretion. Fee terms are set in the client agreement or offering memorandum and are not published: fee schedule not found. The US ADV records 437 individual and high-net-worth accounts, indicating it does take individual clients.
1657428.track_record: No published composite or audited performance was found. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +14.7%, about 4.8 points behind benchmark, on roughly $506M of reported US equity against about US$2.4bn of regulatory AUM, with turnover near 9.5% per quarter.
1657428.good: One of only two firms in this batch genuinely open to individual clients. Long-established, owner-operated, with a diversified quality-compounder approach and modest turnover rather than a single concentrated bet.
1657428.bad: Trailed the benchmark by roughly 4.8 points over our two-year window; publishes no performance record; being a Canadian-domiciled adviser adds cross-border account, custody and tax complexity for a US investor; leadership is thinly documented publicly.
1657428.how_to_engage: The most accessible option in this batch: call 416-865-1867 or use manitouinvestment.com. The stated minimum of about C$2 million sits near or above $1.5M USD but is waivable at the firm's discretion, so ask. Confirm first whether they can accept a US-resident IRA or taxable account at all.

1426398.name: Focused Investors LLC
1426398.who: Los Angeles adviser organized in 2006 and SEC-registered since then, managed by Bruce G. Veaco and Nugroho ('Dede') Soeharto. Veaco previously spent nearly 20 years on the investment team at Pacific Financial Research as principal, portfolio manager and chief financial officer. Runs fully invested, concentrated portfolios of high-quality, mostly US large-cap companies bought at discounts to intrinsic value; about 22 positions with very low turnover.
1426398.terms: One private fund; no individual accounts on the ADV. Per a third-party advisor directory, the fund minimum is $5 million and the separately managed account minimum is $250 million. Fee schedule not found. No public statement found on accepting new clients.
1426398.track_record: No audited or published long-term composite was found; the firm dates to 2006. Our 13F-implied 2-year return: +10.4%, about 9.1 points behind benchmark, on roughly $3.1bn of reported US equity, with turnover of about 3.1% per quarter.
1426398.good: An experienced quality-value process with a genuinely long holding period, run by principals with a long institutional pedigree from Pacific Financial Research.
1426398.bad: The value-tilted book (Goldman Sachs, Johnson & Johnson, Morgan Stanley, Cigna, Disney) lagged our benchmark by roughly 9 points over two years; minimal public disclosure of results; two-person key-person concentration.
1426398.how_to_engage: Minimum exceeds $1.5M. The reported fund minimum of $5 million and SMA minimum of $250 million put this firm out of reach at your size. Only worth a call to 310-734-1200 or focusedinvestors.com if you want to test whether the fund minimum can be waived.

1358706.name: ABRAMS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, L.P.
1358706.who: David Abrams (UPenn history BA) founded Abrams Capital in Boston in 1999 after ~10 years at Seth Klarman's Baupost. Long-term, concentrated value investing across public and private markets and capital structures; ~37 employees (search snippets). Form ADV (filed 3/25/2026): $13.7B discretionary RAUM across 8 private funds (Abrams Capital Partners I/II, Great Hollow International, Riva Capital Partners III-VI, Whitecrest Partners). Firm formerly named Pamet Capital Management.
